sheet-1.description: The map part of sheet 1 lies below the key map and the index of specials and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It forms an L: a strip along the bottom of the sheet and a box at the lower right. It shows Pemberton Road at the western approach to Browns Mills, from a road on the left of the strip to a private road on the right, where the road crosses the Branch of Rancocas Creek on a concrete bridge. North of the road in block 118 is the Browns Mills Silver Fox Ranch, with fox pens, poultry houses, a brooder house and storage sheds, and at its corner on Pemberton Road the Palace Garage with its heater room and gasoline tanks. Along the strip are scattered dwellings, stores and outbuildings, an auto repair shop and Earle's Service Station near the creek. South of the road block 125 is marked exposure and is largely blank. Most of the area is open land; the lot numbers along Pemberton Road (101 to 155) run on into those of sheet 2. The key map above, at 1000 feet to an inch, and the index are not part of this annotation.
notes: The road on the left is taken to be today's Browns Mills Avenue and the private road on the right today's Main Street, from their spacing along Pemberton Road (about 590 m); neither name is printed.
Pemberton Road is today's Pemberton – Browns Mills Road.
The north arrow appears to point about 10 degrees west of true north (magnetic north); the fitted rotation is 14.6 degrees.

Key map of the whole town at 1000 ft (not configured) with index and water/fire notes; the map part is the bottom strip and lower-right box at 100 ft: Pemberton Road at the west end of town, Browns Mills Silver Fox Ranch, Palace Garage, Earle's Service Station, Branch of Rancocas Creek. One part (L-shaped).

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 covers the centre of Browns Mills at 100 feet to an inch, between Pemberton Road at the top and Mirror Lake and Rancocas Creek at the bottom. Lakehurst Avenue and Trenton Road run down the middle and meet just north of the dam, where Lakehurst Road continues south over the creek beside the outlet of Mirror Lake. West of Lakehurst Avenue the streets are mostly laid out but unbuilt: Ashton, Brook, Rancocas Avenue, Hill, Bridge, Smith, Noteboon Avenue and Chapel, several marked not opened, with blocks 3 to 7 and 126 to 128. The largest building is the Pig'n Whistle Inn, with a private water tower and hydrant nearby, and The Manor boarding house stands on Lakehurst Avenue. Between Lakehurst Avenue and Trenton Road are Bank, Church and Winston Way, the Community M.E. Church, the Browns Mills Volunteer Fire Department No. 1 with an electric siren on a steel tower, an auto repair garage and filling station, stores and dwellings. East of Trenton Road are the Public School, The Plaza, the Sycamore Hall Hotel, Pear Avenue and Club House Road along the north shore of Mirror Lake. Buttonwood Farm lies north of Pemberton Road. A pump house and a printing shop stand at the dam. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings, with a few concrete block buildings.
notes: Lakehurst Avenue north of Trenton Road is today's Juliustown Road; Church is Market Street; Noteboon Avenue is Note Boom Avenue; Pemberton Road is Pemberton – Browns Mills Road.
The short Road between Lakehurst Avenue and Trenton Road by the fire department matches today's Buskansky Lane.
Pemberton Road is drawn 33 ft wide against about 48 ft between today's parcels; the drawn width was given to the detector.

Centre of town at 100 ft: Lakehurst Avenue, Trenton Road, Pemberton Road, Bank, Church, Brook, Bridge, Noteboon Avenue, Club House Road, Mirror Lake. Part 1 main map; part 2 strip at the upper right beyond the heavy line (Trenton Road north, Pemberton Avenue).

sheet-2-2.description: The second part of sheet 2 is the strip at the upper right, beyond the heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned to follow Trenton Road, which runs up the strip from Pemberton Avenue at its foot. The strip shows the lots on both sides of Trenton Road north of the junction, numbered 629 to 666, with dwellings, garages, poultry houses and storage sheds in blocks 119 and 120; one building is of brick with a tile roof. The ground beyond the lots on either side is marked no exposure and left blank. Trenton Road continues on sheet 3, where the Deborah Sanatorium stands at Newton. The north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Pemberton Avenue east of Trenton Road is today's Broadway Street.

Placed on a single junction (Trenton Road at Pemberton Avenue, today Trenton Road, Broadway Street and Pemberton – Browns Mills Road) with the atlas scale and the rotation of the drawn lines; low confidence.

Centre of town at 100 ft: Lakehurst Avenue, Trenton Road, Pemberton Road, Bank, Church, Brook, Bridge, Noteboon Avenue, Club House Road, Mirror Lake. Part 1 main map; part 2 strip at the upper right beyond the heavy line (Trenton Road north, Pemberton Avenue).

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 covers the summer colony on the west and south shore of Mirror Lake, east of the town centre, at 100 feet to an inch. In its upper half a regular grid of named flower streets (Iris, Ivy, Peony, Verbena, Clematis and Arbutus) runs between South Brynwood Drive and North Lake Shore Drive, with blocks B-17 to B-23; most lots are vacant and the buildings are small frame summer cottages, several with names such as Lone Pine, Pine Crest and My Shack, and the Union Gospel Tabernacle on Peony. The Canoe Club with its wooden pier and a bath house stand on the shore of Mirror Lake along Club House Road. The lower half, around Eldredge, North Brynwood Drive, Club House Road, Gleeson and Miller, is more irregular, with Brynwood Brook, Little Pine Lake and arms of Mirror Lake cutting through blocks D-1 1/2 to D-5 1/2 and B-24 to B-26; Wisteria and Holly, both not opened, and Butler Court lie to the west. Named cottages include Four Gables, Nichenhiz, Wee House and Little Sunshine. The sheet's title cartouche reads Pa. instead of N.J.
notes: South Brynwood Drive is today's Brynwood Bogs Drive; North Lake Shore Drive in the lower left (Eldredge to Club House Road) is today's East Lakeshore Drive; Eldredge is Eldridge Street.
Club House Road is lettered Culb House Road along the lake shore.
Today's Clubhouse Road and North Brynwood Drive do not follow the drawn lines in the lower half; only the upper grid and Eldridge / East Lakeshore were used for control.
The title cartouche reads Brown's Mills, Pa.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 the large area of North Lake Shore Drive, Brynwood Drive, Club House Road, Eldredge (Iris to Arbutus streets); part 2 the upper-left box (Lakehurst Avenue, Junction Avenue, Columbus Avenue, Mason, Arch, Haines; Mirror Lake dam); part 3 the lower-left box (Deborah Sanatorium, Trenton Road, Newton). Title cartouche says 'Pa.' by mistake.

sheet-3-2.description: The upper-left box of sheet 3 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch at its own rotation, with north to the upper left. It shows Lakehurst Avenue where it runs along the dam at the foot of Mirror Lake, and the streets south of it: South Lake Shore Drive, Columbus Avenue, Dartmouth and Court (both not opened), Junction Avenue, Mason, Arch and Haines, with blocks 129 to 137, 142 and 143. On the lake side are a wooden pier, a canoe house and gasoline tanks. Along Lakehurst Avenue are a printing shop with power plant, a vacant store, a bowling alley and store, a concrete block store and a lumber yard with lumber shed, warehouse and lumber pile. Elsewhere the blocks hold a few frame dwellings and outbuildings; much of the ground is vacant.
notes: Junction Avenue is today's Junction Road; Lakehurst Avenue here is Lakehurst Road; Dartmouth appears to be today's Oxford Street.
Today's Junction Road, Lakehurst Road and South Lakeshore Drive meet at one node, while South Lake Shore Drive is drawn meeting Lakehurst Avenue west of Junction Avenue; it was not used for control.
Control lies along Junction Road and Lakehurst Road only, so the leave-one-out error is large; low confidence.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 the large area of North Lake Shore Drive, Brynwood Drive, Club House Road, Eldredge (Iris to Arbutus streets); part 2 the upper-left box (Lakehurst Avenue, Junction Avenue, Columbus Avenue, Mason, Arch, Haines; Mirror Lake dam); part 3 the lower-left box (Deborah Sanatorium, Trenton Road, Newton). Title cartouche says 'Pa.' by mistake.

sheet-3-3.description: The lower-left box of sheet 3 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper right, and shows Trenton Road north of the town where Newton meets it. The main feature is the Deborah Sanatorium in block 117: a main building of two stories with an open porch, several frame cottages, a pump house and a 5000 gallon water tank on a roof, with chemical extinguishers noted. South of Newton, block 120 holds a dwelling, an auto house and a poultry house; block 119 lies west of Trenton Road. The ground beyond is marked no exposure. Trenton Road continues on sheet 2.
notes: Newton is not in today's street data where it meets Trenton Road; the part has no surviving junction.
Placed from two features drawn on both sheets (a lot line and a block line at the edges of Trenton Road, carried from sheet 2, part 2) and a derived point 300 ft up Trenton Road; low confidence.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 the large area of North Lake Shore Drive, Brynwood Drive, Club House Road, Eldredge (Iris to Arbutus streets); part 2 the upper-left box (Lakehurst Avenue, Junction Avenue, Columbus Avenue, Mason, Arch, Haines; Mirror Lake dam); part 3 the lower-left box (Deborah Sanatorium, Trenton Road, Newton). Title cartouche says 'Pa.' by mistake.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 covers the summer colony east of Mirror Lake at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north is to the left. Press Avenue runs up the middle, crossed by Spruce Avenue, Columbine Avenue, Stanley Avenue (several not opened), Otter Avenue, Arbor Place, Wilton Way, Albion Way, Melrose Way, Clifton Way and Alden Way, and South Lake Shore Drive runs along the west side next to an arm of Mirror Lake; Orchard Avenue appears at the top. Blocks F-26 to F-49 are mostly vacant lots with a few small frame summer cottages, many named: Solitude, Spruce Lodge, Woodside, Hawthorn Cottage, The Laurels, Minola, Oakwood, Jess-Mine, Woodland and The Blue Bird. Wooden piers reach into the lake. A note says buildings marked C are summer cottages.
notes: Spruce Avenue is today's Palm Avenue.
Modern Albion Way, Melrose Way and Clifton Way run at slightly different angles from the drawn streets.

100 ft. Three parts: part 1 the right area (Press Avenue, South Lake Shore Drive, Columbine to Alden Way; north to the left); part 2 the left strip along South Lake Shore Drive (Hawthorne to Orchard Avenue; north to the upper left); part 3 the inset at the bottom (South Lake Shore Drive at Press Avenue and Alden Way; north to the left).

sheet-4-2.description: The left strip of sheet 4 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. South Lake Shore Drive runs down the strip along the east shore of Mirror Lake, and short streets run from it to the east: Hawthorne, Yarrow, Foxglove, Chicory (not opened), Chandler, Exeter, Gentian, Green, Bishop, Filbert Avenue and Orchard Avenue, which crosses an arm of the lake on a wooden foot bridge. Blocks B-64 to B-72, F-21 and F-22 are mostly vacant lots with scattered frame summer cottages, many named: The Navajo, Tall Pines, Idle Hours, Camp Good Day, The Links, Sunset Lodge, Larsamo Lodge, Pine Camp, Glen, Dot, Restalott and Bob-O-Link. Wooden piers reach into the lake from the shore side of the drive.
notes: Control lies along South Lakeshore Drive only; the fit is a first-order polynomial whose scale across the strip is about 5 percent smaller than along it.
Hawthorne / South Lakeshore Drive was excluded (an edge paired with a line inside the street, 9 m off).

100 ft. sheet-4-3.description: The inset at the bottom of sheet 4 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the left. It shows the end of the peninsula between two arms of Mirror Lake, where South Lake Shore Drive turns along the shore and Press Avenue ends on it, with Alden Way running east from Press Avenue. Blocks F-46 and F-47 hold a few frame dwellings and cottages, and the rest of the lots are vacant.
notes: Placed from two hand-picked junctions only (helmert); low confidence.
